subject: Urgent: ArcadiaHealth production 500s / p99 spike — suspected KV eviction HOL blocking

Subject: Production 500s and p99 jump — urgent

Hi Marissa,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 500 errors and p99 latency from our integration around 08:45 PDT. The errors are mostly coming from Redwood inference endpoints (lots of 500s with "kv-eject" in the logs) and a correlated spike in token latency to >1.2s p99. This is impacting our user flows in the triage UI.

We've attached a small zip with screenshots and a trimmed set of logs (arcadia-error-screenshots.zip). Key observations from our side:
- Error rate rose from ~0.1% to 2.8% over ~20 minutes.
- p95 stayed ok, but p99 and tail latency are terrible.
- Issues appear across multiple regions but most pronounced on us-west.

Can you confirm whether this looks like a configuration/eviction issue on your side? We are on a Dedicated pool with arcadia-prod tenant pin. This is P0 for us — please escalate.

Simon

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Production 500s and p99 jump — urgent

Putting quick notes from triage here so it's all in-thread. High level: KV eviction churn spiked at ~08:42; eviction rate correlates tightly with 500s and p99 tail. The pattern looks like prefix-provoked thrash leading to HOL blocking on hot shards.

What I pulled from the cluster:
- Eviction rate (us-west, tenant=arcadia-prod): 1400 evictions/min at peak (baseline ~60).
- Average KV lookup latency jumped from ~0.8ms to ~6.4ms during the spike.
- Hot shard saturation on 2 nodes (concurrent locks waiting, queue backlog visible).
- Prefetch success rate dropped sharply (cold-prefetch ratio up) — suggests prefetch window missed the working set.

Root-cause hypothesis: a traffic shift (lots of small, low-cardinality prefixes) caused the cache working set to oscillate; aggressive evictions cascade into longer KV lookups and batch lane HOL blocking, amplifying tail latency and triggering 500s when the request timeouts hit our service thresholds.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (fastest to implement):
1) Increase tenant KV cache quota for arcadia-prod by 2x (kv.max_entries_arcadia = current * 2). This reduces eviction churn immediately. Risk: higher memory/slot usage on dedicated pool.
2) Enable aggressive-prefix-warmup for arcadia-prod for 30 minutes (kv.prefix_warmup=true, factor=1.5) to rebuild working set proactively.
3) Temporarily lower max_batch_wait_ms for the affected lane from 25ms -> 15ms to reduce head-of-line wait (reduces batching efficiency slightly but cuts HOL tail).
4) If needed, move arcadia-prod traffic to a spare dedicated lane to isolate hot shard pressure.

I attached a trimmed eviction snapshot (kv-eviction-snapshot-20280622.json) with sample keys and eviction counters. I can push changes now if Marissa and Arcadia approve. Rollback is straightforward (revert kv.max_entries and prefix_warmup).

Estimated outcome: we should see p99 drop towards baseline within 10-15 minutes of the change, and 500s should fall back as hot shards return to normal. Note: small risk of increased spend while quota is lifted.

Ben Carter
SRE, Redwood Inference
